title.narrative: Developing agro-value chains for the improved resilience of rural communities

description.narrative: The hostilities between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) started on April 15, 2023, has heavily impacted on an already fragile country making humanitarian needs across Sudan reaching record levels, with 15.8 million people # about a third of the total population # requiring humanitarian assistance and exacerbating the already high levels of unemployment, poverty and food insecurity in the country. As of early May 2023, more than 600 people have been killed and over 5,100 injured according to the Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH). Moreover, nearly a million people have been newly displaced by the conflict, including more than 700,000 people displaced internally and 200,000 who have crossed into neighbouring countries. In this context, the Sudanese agricultural sector and its strategic agricultural value chains represents now even more a crucial driving force for Sudan#s economic resilience and food security. The agricultural economy in eastern Sudan, particularly, has been relatively less affected by the conflict than other areas such as Khartoum and western Sudan, and hence nowadays it presents better operational opportunities for strengthening the resilience of the national food sector.
